articles.title: What is a fjord? A valley with the sea inside
articles.queryIntent: A geographic definition with a short formation explanation; not cruise or travel-booking advice.

sources.name: National Park Service — U-Shaped Valleys, Fjords, and Hanging Valleys
sources.supports: Moving glaciers widen valleys and steepen their sides; a glacial trough occupied by seawater forms a fjord.

sources.name: National Park Service — Kenai Fjords: glacier movement and erosion
sources.type: Official explanation of Kenai Fjords glacial processes
sources.location: Slip Sliding Away; All that the Glacier Leaves Behind
sources.supports: Flowing ice erodes the landscape; rock carried in ice can scratch and gouge bedrock.

sources.name: NOAA — Classifying Estuaries: By Geology, Fjords section
sources.supports: Retreat can expose a trough to seawater, with freshwater inputs as well. Examples extend beyond Norway.

claimLimits: A glacial valley needs seawater occupation to be a fjord; not every U-shaped valley qualifies.
No universal formation duration, salinity, depth or exclusive Norway claim.
The sparse how-formed query is covered naturally within the definition article, not treated as a separate proven opportunity.

art.scope: A conceptual glacial sea inlet, not a photograph or map of a named location.

articles.title: Why did the Titanic sink? How flooding overwhelmed the ship
articles.queryIntent: The historical physical sinking mechanism, rather than the film, a conspiracy or the casualty count.

sources.name: British Wreck Commissioner’s inquiry (1912) — Report on the loss of the steamship Titanic, pages 5, 35 and 45
sources.type: Original British inquiry, U.S. Senate reprint
sources.supports: The historical inquiry records the dates, attributes the collision to excessive speed, and explains progressive flooding above the bulkheads.

sources.name: NOAA Maritime Heritage Program — The 2010 expedition and mapping of Titanic’s wreck
sources.location: Wreck photo-mosaics and detached hull sections
sources.supports: Later mapping documents separated bow and stern sections; it does not establish the iceberg wound geometry.

claimLimits: The inquiry is primary evidence of its own findings, not the final word on all later forensic questions.
No claim that any arbitrary four compartments were safe or exactly five compartments were damaged.
No steel, rivet, lifeboat or movie scene is presented as the proven sole sinking cause.
The inquiry’s obsolete intact-sinking description is not repeated as modern fact.

demand.interpretation: The definition and historical sinking questions recur in the worldwide and U.S. comparisons. UK exact-question data is sparse. Film/movie rising queries are excluded from the rationale.
limits: Each market/chart is separately normalised; indices are not monthly volume and not comparable across countries. Do not sum close variants.
The formation variant is weak/sparse: a displayed zero is not evidence of no searches. It is addressed naturally within the useful fjord definition, not a separate targeted post.
GB exact-question observations are sparse and do not establish strong recurring UK demand.

Worldwide fjord rising film/movie rows and Titanic film rows are explicitly excluded from the justification. Top definition/how-sinking questions and US/Worldwide recurring rows support the actual educational intents.
English query terms do not filter all searchers to English, and Trends matches search terms rather than supplying exact-query monthly counts.
Search-result intent checked via primary educational/governing sources; no current Google organic position or guaranteed ranking is claimed.

sourceAccessLimits: The original inquiry PDF was downloaded from the government archive; relevant scanned pages and its public-domain transcription were checked.
The NOAA expedition page contains a server-side include warning, while the substantive expedition account remains readable.
Unsuccessful USGS and Library of Congress opens were not counted as read sources.
editorialFormat: Two short regular articles, each with four sections, a direct opening answer, contextual links and an optional game invitation.
performanceLimit: Research and access checks do not establish indexing, rankings, visits, account creation or AI citations.
